title: Phone-style viewer: fixed zoom, a few boxes at a time, scroll to the next question on click
userDescription: make the diagram viewer be at a fixed zoom level that renders only three or four nodes on the mermaid diagram at a time, when viewed in the browser, as though it was a mobile app render. can you click on a nodes decision choice, it scrolls the diagram so that the next set of decisions go into view.
goal: - The diagram shows at a fixed zoom, about 3 or 4 boxes tall, in a phone-shaped area
- Clicking an answer scrolls so the next question and its answers are in view
- The Reset button scrolls back to the top
- The current full-picture view is still available with a switch
notInScope: - The real mobile app; task 1 owns it
problemSolvedByTask: Both: the whole diagram is too big, and I want to see how the mobile app will feel if we made moving between precision points feel like animated scrolling
description: index.html renders the whole diagram into #diagram inside #output (overflow: auto) with mermaid.render() and no zoom control; the SVG scales to fit. Click handling lives in the #output click listener: it adds the clicked Q_*_ answer node to chosenAnswers and calls highlightPath(), which uses walkTrail() to find the bright trail and dims the rest. The next question after a click is the last Q_ node in the walkTrail() result. Needed: a phone-shaped viewport (fixed width, fixed height) around the SVG at a fixed scale so 3 or 4 boxes are visible; after each click, find the SVG element for the next question (id contains 'flowchart-<ID>-') and scrollIntoView with smooth behavior so the question and its answer boxes are in view; the Reset button scrolls back to the top; a switch toggles between this phone view and the current full view. Only index.html changes.
tests: Write tests/index.html.test.ts using node:test. It launches headless Chrome with Playwright (executablePath '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome') against a running `bun server.js`, opens the page, picks accountability.mmd, turns on phone view, and asserts: (1) the output frame is a fixed phone-shaped size, (2) only the first few boxes are inside the frame, (3) after clicking the Q_THEM_DONE_SPEAKING_Y box the Q_ANYTHING_I_DO_NOT_UNDERSTAND box is inside the frame, (4) Reset scrolls back to the top. A manual checklist does not count; the test check only counts test files.
